{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABaiJVpg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEIqBI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 10, "title": "Add reusable video and audio output for browser RTL simulations", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL currently compiles and simulates a counter in the browser, but its UI and WASM simulator adapter expose only the `clk`, `reset`, and `count` interface. To demonstrate graphics- or sound-producing RTL (and eventually a hardware SNES implementation), WebRTL needs **reusable browser video and audio outputs**, not SNES-specific emulation code.

## Expected outcome

A user can run synthesizable RTL in the existing **browser-only** pipeline and see the design's video output on a canvas and hear its generated audio through the browser.

Add simple, documented RTL-to-browser output interfaces:
- **Video:** an example module emits pixel/color data and sufficient pixel/frame synchronization metadata; WebRTL renders those pixels via Canvas (or a comparably simple browser API).
- **Audio:** an example module emits PCM samples plus a sample-valid signal; WebRTL buffers and plays those samples using Web Audio, respecting the browser's user-gesture/audio-unlock requirement.
- Make the output adapters reusable for future RTL projects. Do not hardcode graphics or tones in JavaScript.

## Context

- Project vision: #3
- Browser-side compilation and execution: #8
- The existing browser path is YoWASP Yosys -> CXXRTL -> Clang/LLD -> WASM with separate compiler and simulator workers.
- The current C++ board adapter is counter-specific. Extend or make it selectable for the example interfaces without requiring a full multi-file IDE or a general-purpose FPGA peripheral framework.

## Proposed scope

- Define and document minimal synthesizable RTL signal contracts for video and audio, including reset, clock/sample timing, pixel coordinates or stream framing, channel count, sample format, and how values are transferred to the browser.
- Supply small example RTL designs (e.g., a color-bar/test-pattern generator and a simple PCM tone/sample generator). These should prove the displayed pixels and audible samples actually originate from the compiled RTL.
- Adapt the compiled-circuit host boundary so the chosen example's outputs reach the simulator worker and UI efficiently; support batching rather than per-pixel or per-sample UI round trips.
- Render video on an HTML canvas and play audio with Web Audio/AudioWorklet or a suitable buffered implementation. Make Run, Pause, and Reset behave coherently with output/buffer state.
- Preserve the existing counter demo and browser-side compilation workflow.
- Keep the static GitHub Pages deployment; no remote compiler or SNES ROM is needed.

## Out of scope

- Implementing a SNES CPU/PPU/APU, loading commercial game ROMs, or claiming SNES real-time performance.
- Emulating HDMI, analog video/audio electrical behavior, physical devices, or cycle-accurate DAC characteristics.
- Full multi-file project management, arbitrary pin mapping, or a generic peripheral plugin ecosystem.
- High-performance GPU rendering, complex audio processing, or guaranteeing real-time throughput for large RTL designs.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The browser can compile and execute an RTL video test-pattern example; canvas pixels visibly follow **the compiled RTL outputs**. Changing the RTL pattern changes the displayed image after recompilation.
- [ ] The browser can compile and execute an RTL audio example; its PCM samples are delivered to Web Audio and are audibly played after a user gesture. Changes to the RTL samples/frequency affect playback.
- [ ] Video framing/timing and audio sample format/rate are documented and tested; simulation time and playback time are handled explicitly rather than implicitly equated to JavaScript timer speed.
- [ ] Worker-to-UI delivery uses bounded buffers/batching and does not require synchronous UI calls for every pixel or audio sample.
- [ ] Run/Pause/Reset work without accumulating stale frame/audio data; errors and missing browser audio permission are handled gracefully.
- [ ] Existing browser counter compile/step/reset behavior remains functional.
- [ ] The features work from the GitHub Pages-compatible static build (no backend), and automated or reproducible checks verify output derives from edited RTL rather than from browser-side fake generators.
- [ ] The RTL I/O contracts, example usage, supported browsers, performance limitations, and audio-unlock behavior are documented.

## Optional validation

- Benchmark simulated cycles/second and video frames/audio samples per wall-clock second.
- Validate on additional browsers, and explore gamepad/ROM/memory input adapters as separate follow-up tasks.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, check the public GitHub Pages site loads the video example, displays the pattern, and plays the audio example after a user gesture. Record actual results separately; public deployment verification is not a pre-merge condition.

## Related

- #3 — Overall project vision
- #8 — Browser-only compilation and simulation
